title: Error handling & fault resilience
literature: Preschern error-handling patterns (Fluent C); Nygard Release It! (stability patterns); POSA3; exception-safety (Sutter Exceptional C++); Erlang/OTP supervision.

members.name: Brown-Out Handling
members.what: Detect supply voltage sagging below a safe threshold (via an on-chip or external detector) and hold the MCU in reset or run a controlled shutdown until power is reliable.

members.name: Built-In Self-Test
members.what: Firmware routines that exercise and verify the system's own hardware (RAM patterns, ROM checksums, register/ALU checks, peripheral loopbacks) at startup or periodically.

members.name: Circuit Breaker
members.what: A stateful wrapper around a failure-prone operation that trips open after a failure threshold, rejects calls while open, and probes recovery via a half-open state.

members.name: Cleanup Record
members.what: A variable records which acquisition steps succeeded so a single cleanup path can conditionally release exactly what was obtained.

members.name: Complete Parameter Checking
members.what: Validate all parameters and inputs at component boundaries every time, detecting errors close to their source at the cost of some performance.

members.name: Copy-and-Swap
members.what: Implement assignment by constructing a copy and swapping its guts with *this via a non-throwing swap, so the operation either fully succeeds or leaves the object untouched.

members.name: Core Dump
members.what: On a fatal fault, a handler serializes the program's execution state (registers, stack, selected memory regions, fault status) to persistent storage or a host channel for postmortem analysis.

members.name: Correcting Audits
members.what: Routinely scan in-memory or stored data for structural and semantic errors and repair them (rebuild links, reset invalid fields) as they are found.

members.name: Cyclic Redundancy Check
members.what: Data blocks carry a checksum computed by polynomial division over GF(2); the receiver/reader recomputes it to detect corruption in storage or transit.

members.name: Dead Letter Channel
members.what: A designated channel to which the messaging layer moves messages that cannot be delivered or processed, instead of dropping or endlessly retrying them.

members.name: Deferred Validation
members.what: Delay comprehensive validity checking of captured data until an action requires it, scaling the rigor of the check to the consequences of that action (edit freely, validate on save/commit/publish).

members.name: Diagnostic Context
members.what: Attach per-thread/per-request key-value context (transaction id, user, request id) to a stash that the logging system automatically appends to every message emitted within that scope.

members.name: Diagnostic Logger
members.what: Route all diagnostic messages through a dedicated logger object that decouples message producers from output destinations, formats, and severity filtering.

members.name: Error Handler
members.what: Concentrate error-processing logic in dedicated handler components/blocks separate from normal-flow code, invoked when errors are detected.

members.name: Error Kernel
members.what: Keep the irreplaceable state and critical logic in a small, maximally simple core, delegating risky or failure-prone work to expendable child components that can crash and be restarted.

members.name: Escalation
members.what: When a recovery action fails to clear an error, escalate to a progressively more drastic action (retry -> restart task -> restart process -> reboot) up a defined ladder.

members.name: Exceptional Value
members.what: A distinguished value object representing missing or invalid input that flows through the domain model, absorbing or rejecting messages instead of raising errors.

members.name: Fail Fast
members.what: Check preconditions and resource availability up front and report failure immediately, rather than doing work that is doomed to fail slowly.

members.name: Goto Cleanup
members.what: On failure, jump forward to a single labeled cleanup section at the end of the function that releases resources in reverse acquisition order.

members.name: Guard Clause
aka: replace nested conditional with guard clauses
members.what: Check preconditions/special cases at the top of a function and return immediately, keeping the main path unindented.

members.name: Happy Eyeballs
members.what: Race connection attempts over alternative paths (canonically IPv6 vs IPv4) with small staggered delays, keep the first to succeed, and cancel the rest.

members.name: Heartbeat
members.what: A monitored component emits (or answers) a periodic signal; missing beats mark it as failed and trigger recovery.

members.name: Leaky Bucket Counter
members.what: An error counter incremented on each fault and decremented ('leaked') periodically; recovery escalates only when the count crosses a threshold, i.e. errors arrive faster than they drain.

members.name: Let It Crash
members.what: On unexpected error, abandon in-process recovery: let the failing unit die immediately and rely on an external mechanism (supervisor, restart) to recreate it in a known-good state.

members.name: Log Errors
members.what: Record error details on a separate diagnostic channel (log file, console, trace buffer) at the point where the error occurs, instead of forcing all debug information through return values to the caller.

members.name: Loop Timeout
members.what: Bound every polling/wait loop with a software counter or hardware timer so the loop cannot hang forever if the awaited hardware condition never occurs.

members.name: Marked Data
members.what: Tag data elements known or suspected to be erroneous so subsequent processing can skip, repair, or handle them specially instead of propagating the corruption.

members.name: Meaningless Behavior
members.what: Write domain methods without defensive input checks; let computations on exceptional/missing values fail or yield meaningless results, and have the input/output boundary recover (e.g. display blank) instead.

members.name: N-Version Programming
members.what: Run N independently developed implementations of the same specification and adjudicate their outputs by a voter to mask residual design faults.

members.name: Notification
members.what: An object that accumulates errors and messages during an operation (typically validation) and is returned or passed across a layer boundary instead of throwing on first failure.

members.name: Quarantine
members.what: Isolate a faulty element from the rest of the system - stop routing work to it, fence its outputs - so its errors cannot spread while diagnosis or recovery proceeds.

members.name: Railway-Oriented Programming
members.what: Composing a workflow as a chain of functions over a two-track success/failure type, where any failure switches the rest of the pipeline onto the error track automatically.

members.name: Recovery Blocks
members.what: Execute a primary algorithm, validate its result with an acceptance test, and on failure roll back and run an alternate implementation of the same function.

members.name: Restart
members.what: Recover from an unhandled or unrecoverable error by reinitializing the affected unit (task, process, component, or whole program) to its known-good initial state.

members.name: Result Type
members.what: A sum type carrying either a success value or an error value, returned instead of throwing, so failure is part of the function's signature.

members.name: Retry Budget
members.what: Cap retries globally as a fraction of primary requests (e.g. retries may add at most 10% extra load), disabling retry when the budget is exhausted.

members.name: Retry with Exponential Backoff and Jitter
members.what: Retry a failed operation a bounded number of times, doubling the wait between attempts and randomizing (jittering) it to avoid synchronized retry storms.

members.name: Return Status Code
members.what: Functions return a numeric/enum status indicating success or a specific failure, delivering actual results through out-parameters.

members.name: Riding Over Transients
members.what: Deliberately ignore errors that are momentary and self-clearing, acting only when an error persists or recurs beyond a threshold.

members.name: Roll-Forward
members.what: Recover from an error by advancing the system to a new consistent state ahead of the error point, reconstructing or discarding in-flight work rather than returning to a checkpoint.

members.name: Rollback
members.what: Recover from an error by restoring the system to a previously saved consistent state (a checkpoint) and resuming from there.

members.name: Safe State
members.what: A predefined operating condition without unreasonable risk that the system deliberately enters on fault detection (outputs de-energized, actuators parked, subsystem disabled).

members.name: Samurai Principle
aka: return victorious or not at all
members.what: For errors the caller cannot meaningfully handle, do not return an error code - assert/abort at the failure point instead.

members.name: Sentinel Value
members.what: A special in-band value, distinct from all legal data, used to signal a condition such as end-of-data, absence, or failure (NUL terminator, -1, null pointer).

members.name: setjmp/longjmp Error Handling
members.what: Macro-wrapped setjmp/longjmp implementing raise-and-catch non-local control transfer as an exception facility in C.

members.name: Software Rejuvenation
members.what: Proactively restart or reinitialize a long-running process on a schedule or on resource-degradation signals, before software aging (leaks, fragmentation, drift) causes failure.

members.name: Special Return Value
members.what: Reserve one or more values of the normal return domain (NULL, -1, EOF) to signal failure in-band, avoiding a separate status channel.

members.name: Stack Painting / Watermarking
members.what: Fill each stack with a known pattern at startup and later scan for the deepest overwritten address to measure worst-case stack usage and detect near-overflow.

members.name: Supervisor
members.what: A component whose only job is to monitor child workers and apply a declared restart strategy (one-for-one, one-for-all, escalation to its own supervisor) when they crash.

members.name: Timeout
members.what: Bound every blocking wait on an external resource or call with a maximum duration, treating expiry as failure.
